name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
summary: A unilateral free-weight pull where the torso is supported by a flat bench while rowing a dumbbell to the hip to train the back musculature.

setup: Place one knee and the corresponding hand firmly on a flat bench to support your upper body, keeping your supporting arm under your shoulder.
Plant your opposite foot firmly on the floor slightly behind you with a stable, wide base.
Maintain a flat, neutral spine roughly parallel to the floor.
Grasp the dumbbell on the floor with your free hand using a neutral grip, letting your arm hang fully extended.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blade and driving your elbow back toward your hip.
Pull the dumbbell upward in a slight arc until your elbow passes your torso and the dumbbell reaches your lower rib cage.
Pause briefly at the top of the contraction without twisting your torso.
Lower the dumbbell under control along the same path until the arm is fully extended and the lat is stretched.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you row the dumbbell toward your hip, and inhale as you lower it back to full extension.
cues: Drive the elbow to the hip
Keep your chest parallel to the floor
Pull with your back, not your hand

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso rotation to heave the weight up.
common_faults.correction: Brace your core and keep your shoulders and hips square to the bench throughout the set.

common_faults.fault: Rowing the dumbbell straight up to the chest instead of back toward the hip.
common_faults.correction: Focus on driving the elbow backward in an arcing motion rather than pulling directly upward with the bicep.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the bottom range of motion short.
common_faults.correction: Allow the scapula to protract slightly and the arm to reach full extension at the bottom for a deep lat stretch.

precautions: Avoid rounding the lower back while supporting your weight on the bench.
Ensure your foot on the floor is placed firmly to resist rotational forces.
